question: why does canonical-layout L1 NOT reproduce legacy L1 on metaqa (paired overlap 1370: BASE ALL@P50 legacy 0.6898 vs canonical 0.5168, McNemar p ~ 0)?
finding: the retrieval channel changed regime. Legacy metaqa nodes were encoded as name + verbalised KB triples (display name + up to 10 kb.txt triples, src/pipeline/loaders.py load_metaqa), so dense/SPLADE could match an answer movie from an actor question. The canonical corpus stores text == the exact entity name (SOURCE_CONTRACT NORMALIZATION_RULE: 'Triple verbalization ... is a downstream ENCODING choice, not corpus identity') and the served encodings (gte-Qwen2-1.5B dense, SPLADE) were computed on that bare name, so the top-200 caches retrieve name-similar entities only (actor question -> other actors named Tom). Gold answers enter the P50 scope only through the structural/partition hop from the topic entity.

legacy_node_content_example.content: Kismet. Kismet directed by William Dieterle | Kismet written by Edward Knoblock | Kismet starred actors Marlene Dietrich | ... | Kismet release year 1944 | Kismet in language English | Kismet has tags bd-r

canonical_text_rule: Stored text = the EXACT official entity name. No NFC/NFKC, no casefolding, no whitespace collapsing, no stripping, no '_'->' '. text == title == entity name. The legacy lossy collapse (strip().lower().replace('_',' '), which merged 3,083 distinct-case entities down to 40,151) is NOT reproduced; it is quantified only, in identity_normalization_diagnostics. Triple verbalization (display name + up to 10 kb.txt triples) is a downstream ENCODING choice, not corpus identity.
webqsp_same_axis: webqsp canonical entity nodes are NAME_ONLY too (ALL_NODE__entity_NAME_ONLY default arm; CVT records carry the facts); V1_RETRIEVAL_ROLE_DECISION.json OPEN_AXIS_NOT_DECIDED_HERE: 'entity text = NAME_ONLY vs NAME_PLUS_FACTS -- NOT settled'. The legacy 781k webqsp substrate was verbalised name + <=15 relations. So the legacy KB-corpus L1 numbers (metaqa, webqsp) are not reproducible on the canonical encodings by construction; text corpora (squad, musique, hotpotqa, 2wiki) encode passages on both sides.
not_an_L1_bug: hypergraph builder parity 6/6 IDENTICAL, replay-cache builder parity 4/4 IDENTICAL on the legacy inputs; the difference is in the served encodings' text, i.e. a substrate encoding ruling, not L1 code.
ruling_needed: KEEP NAME_ONLY: canonical KB-corpus L1 is a different regime (retrieval finds topic entities, structure must reach answers); legacy metaqa/webqsp L1 cells become historical comparison points on a different encoding, not baselines to match

NAME_PLUS_FACTS for KB corpora: re-encode metaqa (43,234 short texts -- small) and webqsp entities (925,761 READABLE + 62,375 MID-named) with the frozen encoders, rebuild the two retrieval caches, supersede CANONICAL_FREEZE for those channels; needs a GPU (Modal dead)
